blog.title: Spring release notes
blog.excerpt: A short note on the bowls, cups, and surface tests that shaped this small release.
blog.body:
This release gathers the quieter pieces from the last firing: low bowls, handled cups, and vessels with surfaces that keep a record of the kiln. The goal is functional work that still carries the pace of the studio.

Most pieces were made one at a time and held back until the glaze felt settled. Expect small differences in rim line, iron speckling, and pooling; those shifts are part of the work rather than defects.

blog.title: What the glaze kept
blog.excerpt: Notes from a wall tile study and a pair of ridge vessels after a slower round of surface testing.
blog.body:
The wall tile tests started as a way to watch how a thin clear glaze pools over pressed clay. The best surfaces held enough variation to reward a second look without becoming too loud.

That same restraint carried into the ridge vessel pair. The ribbing catches shadow first, then the dry matte surface gives the form a little gravity.
